comparison: Both address the histidine tag artifact (C41-C42). OpenEval finds the characterization SUPPORTED, noting the authors appropriately traced and reproduced the artifact. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, expressing concern that a version without the tag needs to be generated and an alternative normalization design is required.

Both address the discrepancy between in vitro Kd and cellular measurements (C74). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree this is UNCERTAIN, with OpenEval noting the compartmentalization explanation is speculative without direct evidence, and peer reviewers noting that information on subcellular aspartate dynamics remains incomplete.

Both address temporal dynamics of aspartate depletion (C75). OpenEval and peer reviewers both find this SUPPORTED, with OpenEval noting the practical importance of showing different treatments reach steady state at different times, and peer reviewers accepting the temporal dynamics data without critique.

Both address in vitro characterization (C3-C5, C33, C37) with partial overlap on temperature/pH sensitivity (C43, C45). OpenEval finds all claims SUPPORTED by dose-response curves and specificity testing. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, describing characterization as 'convincing' and noting the sensor is not affected by temperature.

Both address correlation between sensor fluorescence and LCMS measurements (C71-C72). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED, calling it 'critical validation' with strong correlation data. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, describing the functional characterization as 'convincing' and accepting the correlation without critique.

Both address recovery kinetics and cell proliferation (C54-C57). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with clear documentation of multi-phase recovery and correlation with proliferation. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting additional cell viability data after 60 hours of treatment.

Both address the rational design approach and specificity-switching mutations (C31-C32, with peer also addressing C79). OpenEval finds the strategy SUPPORTED based on crystal structure and bacterial lysate screening. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, accepting the structurally guided amino acid substitution approach without critique.

Both address asparagine supplementation during glutamine starvation (C69-C70). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED though notes the interpretation remains somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, highlighting it as 'one of the highlights of the manuscript' demonstrating sensor utility.

Both address pH sensitivity (C45). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED, noting aspartate-induced changes exceed pH effects with appropriate data. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, requesting additional validation using an untagged version coupled to a pH sensor in cultured cells.

OpenEval R8 addresses rotenone and pyruvate rescue temporal dynamics (C47-C49). Peer R2 addresses broader cellular validation including these claims plus others (C6-C9, C51, C54-C55, C61, C65). Both find the temporal dynamics measurements SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers describing the characterization as 'convincing' and highlighting successful establishment of temporal dynamics.

OpenEval R18 addresses broad utility across genetic, pharmacological, and nutritional manipulations (C7-C9). Peer R2 covers overlapping cellular validation claims. Both find this SUPPORTED, with OpenEval noting comprehensive demonstration of sensor utility and peer reviewers noting 'different strategies were used to bring aspartate to the minimal level.'

OpenEval R9 addresses GOT1/2 knockout validation (C50-C53). Peer R2 includes C51 among broader cellular validation claims. Both find the genetic validation SUPPORTED, with OpenEval noting the genetic system provides a clean test of sensor ability to detect aspartate depletion.

OpenEval R11 addresses metformin differential kinetics (C58-C61). Peer R2 includes C61 among broader cellular validation. Both find this SUPPORTED, with OpenEval noting the differential kinetics observation is novel and demonstrates sensor utility for comparing drug effects over time.

OpenEval R12 addresses BAM15 rescue experiment (C62-C65). Peer R2 includes C65 among broader cellular validation. Both find this SUPPORTED, with OpenEval noting the experiment confirms prior observations using the new sensor.

OpenEval R1 addresses background literature establishing biological context and importance of aspartate metabolism (C1-C2, C15-C28). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these introductory/background claims were not specifically evaluated by peer reviewers.

OpenEval R2 addresses known limitations of mass spectrometry and advantages of biosensors (C10-C14). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these methodological motivation claims were not specifically evaluated by peer reviewers.

OpenEval R7 addresses sensor response to metabolic perturbations and RFP normalization stability (C46). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this specific validation experiment was not separately evaluated by peer reviewers.

OpenEval R17 addresses comparison to concurrent work by Hellweg et al. (C76-C82), including differences in engineering approach, performance characteristics, and specificity validation. Peer R8 only minimally overlaps (C79). OpenEval finds the comparison SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats; peer reviewers accepted the engineering approach but did not specifically evaluate the comparative claims.
